texts.preamble: State vs Sunil Kumar on 17 September, 2024 In The Court Of Judicial Magistrate First Class- 08 (Central), Tis Hazari Courts : Delhi Presiding Officer: Ms. Sayesha Chadha, Djs Fir No. 187/13 Ps : Kamla Market U/s 279/304A Ipc & 6 Dmvr/177 Mv Act State vs. Sunil Kumar Date of Institution of case : 11.03.2014 Date when Judgment reserved : 29.07.2024 Date on which Judgment pronounced : 17.09.2024 Judgment A. Case No. : 290563/16 B. Date of Institution of Case : 11.03.2014 C. Date of Commission of Offence : 17.11.2013 D. Name of the complainant : Mohd.Amzad Ali E. Name of the Accused : Sunil Kumar s/o Sh. Chet & his parentage and residence Ram, R/o Village Shaharmalpur, Tehsil Samalkha, District Panipat, Haryana. F. Offences complained of : U/s 279/304A Indian Penal Code and 6 DMVR/177 MV Act G. Plea of the Accused : Pleaded not guilty H. Final order : Conviction I. Date of such order : 17.09.2024 State Vs. Sunil Kumar PS Kamla Market
texts.facts: The case of prosecution in brief is that on 17.11.2013 at about 08:30 AM, at Ajmeri Gate Chowk, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Kamla Market, accused was driving DTC bus bearing registration no. DL1PC 9479, in such a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and accused was found without valid badge and while driving the aforesaid vehicle accused caused the death of pedestrian namely Heeramani who was crossing the road which is not amounting to culpable homicide and thereby committing an offence punishable u/s 279/304A Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter called as IPC). State vs Sunil Kumar on 17 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16669663/ 1 2. Upon conclusion of investigation, a final report was filed before the court on 11.03.2014 against the accused. Cognizance of offence punishable u/s 279/304A IPC was taken. Upon summoning, the accused appeared and copies of charge sheet were supplied to the accused in compliance of Section 207 of The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter called as Cr.P.C). Thereafter, notice for offence punishable u/s 279/304A IPC and 6 DMVR/177 MV Act was framed against the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and opted for trial. There was no bus except the offending bus on the road at the time of incident. He was managing the traffic and stopped the vehicles, coming from wrong side. The offending bus was coming from the opposite road, on which he was standing. The accused hit the injured on the red light. The wind screen/front glass of the offending bus was broken by the accident. The victim sustained injuries on his head. He was not able to recollect which mobile number he was carrying on the date of incident. The offending vehicle was taken/parked on the side of the road after the accident by the driver.

Rash and negligent driving has to be examined in light of the facts and circumstances of a given case.
It is a fact incapable of being construed or seen in isolation.
It must be examined in light of the attendant circumstances.
A person who drives a vehicle on the road is liable to be held responsible for the act as well as for the result.
It may not be always possible to determine with reference to the speed of a vehicle whether a person was driving rashly and negligently.
Both these acts presuppose an abnormal conduct.
Even when one is driving a vehicle at a slow speed but recklessly and negligently, it would amount to 'rash and negligent driving' within the meaning of the language of Section 279 IPC.
That is why the legislature has used the words 'manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life'.

Negligence is not an absolute term but is a relative one;
it is rather a comparative term.
It is difficult to state with precision any mathematically exact formula by which negligence or lack of it can be infallibly measured in a given case.

Whether there exists negligence per se or the course of conduct amounts to negligence will normally depend upon the attending and surrounding facts and circumstances which have to be taken into consideration by the Court.

In a given case, even not doing what one was ought to do can constitute State vs Sunil Kumar on 17 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16669663/
9 negligence.
The Court has to adopt another parameter, i.e., 'reasonab

The doctrine of reasonable care imposes an obligation or a duty upon a person (for example a driver) to care for the pedestrian on the road and this duty attains a higher degree when the pedestrian happen to be children of tender years.

It is axiomatic to say that while driving a vehicle on a public way, there is an implicit duty cast on the drivers to see that their driving does not endanger the life of the right users of the road, may be either vehicular users or pedestr
They are expected to take sufficient care to avoid danger to others".
28. Hence, it is the duty of the driver of the alleged vehicle to observe a reasonable duty of care while driving on the route.

It is an implicit duty on the driver to check that their driving does not State Vs.
